risk_reasons: Changes an auto-approval gate: readiness `autopilotAvailable` drops `autopilotPurchasable()`, so an Autopilot account may widen auto-approval while the Autopilot sale is paused.
Changes owner-facing copy on the Owner Operator Proposal card, which sits directly on the `auto_approval_policies` Apply path even though this change writes nothing.
Corrects an owner-facing claim about whether replies reach Google; a wrong correction is itself a false statement to the owner.
goal: An owner whose account carries a Posting block is told so by the Owner Operator - in the turn reply and on the Proposal card - instead of being told the auto-reply rule is live.
non_goals: Judge health (`isJudgeHealthy`) stays out; the Posting block reports configured eligibility only.
The per-location gates `archived_location` and `active_zernio_connection_missing` stay out.
Every per-draft gate (moderation, triage, rating, daily cap, review hash) stays out.
The Operator does not refuse to prepare or Apply a policy change while a Posting block is present.
No change to `evaluateAutoApprovalCandidate` or the publisher Judge gate; posting behaviour itself is untouched.
No new feature flag and no new env var.
No change to the `/settings/auto-approval` headline logic beyond importing the shared copy map.
user_visible_behavior: When the account carries a Posting block and the policy would otherwise read as armed, the Operator reply states the account is not set up to post automatically right now and names each block reason in owner language.
The Operator says 'set to post', never 'posts', matching the settings headline.
A Proposal card for a policy operation that arms auto-posting shows one server-written line per Posting block reason, using the same sentences as /settings/auto-approval.
An Autopilot account may widen auto-approval while AUTOPILOT_PURCHASABLE is false; readiness no longer reports `autopilot_unavailable` for it.
A Copilot account still carries `autopilot_unavailable` in readiness and still cannot widen auto-approval.
The owner can still change or turn off auto-reply settings through the Operator while a Posting block is present.
invariants: Invariant #3: no code path in this change approves or posts anything.
Invariant #13: no NEXT_PUBLIC_* companion; the Posting block reaches the browser through server responses only.
Invariant #14: the Operator never reads `auto_approval_policies` from client code.
Invariant #15: `buildSnapshot` keeps its explicit `db` parameter and `src/lib/agents/operator/` never imports @/lib/db/server.
The Context snapshot carries no review text, no response text and no reviewer name.
ci:pool-fanout: the reads in `buildSnapshot` stay sequential; no Promise combinator over DB-issuing elements.
The Operator's posting claim is derived only from `posting.blocked` / `posting.reasons`, never from readiness.
Each owner-facing Posting block sentence has exactly one owner: the shared copy module.
Readiness keeps answering 'may the owner widen auto-approval?' and the Posting block keeps answering 'is this account set up to post?'; the two stay distinct values.
edge_cases: Account default off and no override armed, with a Posting block present: the Operator says off, not a correction - the settings rule at AutoApprovalClient.tsx:726 that a block must not turn a true sentence into a correction.
Account default off with one location override armed and a Posting block present: the correction fires.
Policy suspended AND Posting block present: suspension wording wins and the block line still appears exactly once.
Missing account row: `autopilot_tier_required` and `publisher_subscription_denied` are both present and both stated.
Autopilot tier with AUTOPILOT_PURCHASABLE=false: no Posting block and, after this change, no `autopilot_unavailable`.
Copilot tier: `autopilot_tier_required` in posting and `autopilot_unavailable` in readiness are both present and are different sentences about different questions.
Runtime flag off: readiness still reports `auto_approval_disabled`, because `autopilotPurchasable()` was not the only reader of that flag.

The Posting block clears between Proposal preparation and the card render: the line is derived at READ time from the current settings response, so it clears with the block and is never stale. This deliberately differs from `expansionBlockedBy`, which is frozen at preparation because it gates Apply; this line gates nothing.
Several reasons at once: every reason is listed, in the fixed `buildAutoApprovalPostingStatus` order.

rollback_plan: Revert the merge commit. There is no migration, no new flag and no new env var, so revert restores both the Operator wording and the previous readiness entitlement in one step. AUTOPILOT_PURCHASABLE keeps its own meaning throughout and needs no change either way.
observability: GET /api/settings/auto-approval readiness.blockReasons for an Autopilot account: `autopilot_unavailable` disappears while AUTOPILOT_PURCHASABLE is false. This is the single externally checkable signal of the entitlement change.
Operator turn logs already carry the turn id and correlation id; no new signal is added.
